title: Rosalind and the Verdict
premise: Coral Joubert, the meticulous archivist of Saint-Aubin's cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger named Rosalind Verne to prove that a murder scheduled for the coming solstice will not happen — a crime recorded in a thirty-year-old ledger entry Coral himself filed and forgot. Following the crypt's sealed records, Coral discovers the 'future murder' is a ritual of institutional memory: each generation, the cathedral's ruling chapter erases one inconvenient person from its books, and this year the chosen victim is Rosalind. To save her, Coral must weaponize his own archive against the men who taught him invisibility, ending with him unlocking the crypt publicly, restoring every erased name — including his mother's — at the cost of his position, as the town finally confronts what its orderly silence purchased.
about_author: Lena Okonkwo is a former parish records clerk who spent six years cataloguing documents no one was meant to read. She writes mysteries about the violence hidden inside tidy systems.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A woman calling herself Rosalind Verne hires Coral to prove her murder won't occur, paying triple and citing a ledger entry dated three decades past. Coral, professionally skeptical, checks his own files and finds the entry — in his own handwriting, though he never wrote it. Emotional beat: unease; the archivist realizes his perfect system contains something he cannot account for.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Missing
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Cross-referencing old burial registers, Coral finds gaps — names removed mid-alphabet, pages re-sewn. The cathedral's canon treasurer warns him off with friendly menace. Rosalind reveals she's the granddaughter of a woman erased in 1994, and the 'murder' is a recurring rite of deletion. Emotional beat: dread deepening into resolve as Coral recognizes his complicity.

chapters.title: Locked Crypt, Open Wounds
chapters.summary: POV Coral. On the solstice eve, Coral breaks into the crypt and finds the chapter's true ledger: a list of erased townspeople, his mother among them, each deletion signed by successive deans. He's caught by the treasurer, offered partnership in the silence. Emotional beat: climax of temptation — survival offered at the price he's paid all his life.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Verdict
chapters.summary: POV Coral. At the solstice service, Coral reads the erased names aloud from the pulpit, unlocks the crypt before the congregation, and hands the ledger to a journalist. The chapter collapses; Rosalind's grandmother's name is recarved in stone. Coral loses his post but gains a self no longer alphabetized away. Emotional beat: costly, quiet vindication.
